judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare insuring promise to pay 'the proceeds of this Policy according to the following provisions'; the operative content is all delegated elsewhere, so there is little in the words themselves to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly subordinates itself to Sections 3-10 (Proceeds is defined in 2.5 and computed in Section 4), so it harmonises rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard free-look right: return within 20 days of receipt and the policy is void from the beginning with premium refunded; the only softness is the undefined trigger date of 'receipt'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 3.1 (no coverage until premium paid) and 7.2 (effective date) without contradiction, since a returned policy is void ab initio.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The automatic paid-up conversion at the anniversary following the Insured's 95th birthday is stated in truncated conditional form ('level amount based on the current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness'), leaving the actual paid-up amount indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section 4.2's Coverage Option A/B death benefit, the Section 1 maturity date and the Section 5.4 cost-of-insurance table that runs to age 94, and the fit is not obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An orientation paragraph telling the reader that Sections 3-10 give 'a more complete description of these rights than is possible to include here'; nothing operative turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It functions as a soft priority rule subordinating Section 2 definitions to the operative sections, which could matter if a definition (e.g. 2.15's cross-reference) diverges from the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line identification of the Insured as the person listed in Section 1 whose death causes proceeds to be paid; definite as far as it goes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.2 (Owner may be someone other than the Insured) and Section 1, which names Lori Antonio as both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain definitional equation of 'you' with the Owner, expressly allowing the Owner to differ from the Insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Sections 8.1-8.3 on ownership and change of ownership; no competing usage of 'you' appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the insurer; there is nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout; no rival definition anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition survives only in fragment ('as named in the original application but may subsequently be changed'), so the mechanism for change is not visible on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 supplies the default that the Owner is beneficiary if none is named and governs changes, so 2.4 is incomplete relative to 8.4 rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining Proceeds as the amount payable both on death and 'upon surrender of the Policy while this Policy is in force and the Insured is alive' packs two very different payables into one term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 pays 'Surrender Value' on surrender and 'Death Proceeds' on death, and Section 10 speaks of 'Policy Proceeds', so the terms overlap imperfectly across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely mechanical anchor date for months, years and anniversaries, keyed to Section 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistently used by 2.17, 5.10 and 7.2; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines Effective Date as 'the date coverage commences' and then routes the reader to three different places for three different coverages, which is a pointer rather than a rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 3.1 ('no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made') and 7.2 (later of Policy Date or premium payment), and those two are not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment of the age definition survives ('upon the Insured's age on the birthday nearest the first...'), so the measuring convention is not fully stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Age drives the 4.2 corridor table and the 5.4 cost-of-insurance table, both of which assume a determinate 'correct age', so an incomplete age rule has downstream reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the Planned Periodic Premium is what the Owner 'most recently elects' yet also that the Section 1 figure 'is the minimum that must be paid' in the first two years, and predicts premiums 'may, in turn, affect the amount and duration of insurance coverage' in loose terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 3.2(1)-(2) and with the first-two-year no-lapse rule in 5.10, and whether the Section 1 amount is a floor or merely a plan is worked out differently in those places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: the Minimum Initial Premium is shown in Section 1 and must be paid before delivery.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 says it must be paid 'at or before' delivery and 7.2 keys the effective date to the date of payment, so 'before' versus 'at or before' is a small but real divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is truncated mid-sentence, leaving 'the amount you specified in the original application' hanging against its role in determining the death benefit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2 supplies the increase/decrease machinery and 5.9 reduces the Specified Amount on withdrawals under Option A, so the definition is a pointer that depends on those sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Death Benefit as the amount payable 'prior to any adjustment specified in Section 4', which is definitional deferral rather than ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 does the work and 5.4 uses 'death benefit on the prior Monthly Due Date' in the cost-of-insurance formula, so the term is used in at least two senses (gross versus adjusted).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — an increased death benefit 'when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size' — states no minimum and is vague on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2's corridor percentages supply the actual rule, so the vagueness is curable by cross-reference, though the two do not use the same vocabulary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition itself is clear: the monthly deduction covering cost of insurance plus rider costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs the reader to 'Section 4.3', but the Monthly Insurance Charge is actually described in Section 5.3 (and 4.3 is Interest on Death Proceeds) — a cross-reference that does not fit the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Cost of Insurance as the charge for 'pure insurance protection' at current rates and excludes rider costs; 'pure insurance protection' is a term of art but is given content by 5.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to 5.4 is correct and 5.3 adds rider costs on top, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes the Monthly Due Date as the same day of each month as the Policy Date; mechanical and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.3, 5.10 and 4.2's use of the 'Monthly Due Date prior to or coinciding with' the date of death.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The flat statement that 'there is no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' is absolute and one-sided, and the OCR-scrambled first line makes the required payment ('Planned Periodic Premium or Minimum Initial Premium') read as a choice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2 contemplates coverage keyed to a Temporary Insurance Agreement given when the premium was taken, which sits awkwardly against an absolute no-coverage-until-payment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in permitting premiums 'at any time and in any amount you choose subject to the following'; the qualification is expressly signalled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four numbered conditions that follow, plus 3.3's premium cap, are the promised limits, so the structure coheres.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text survives only as a fragment; the operative requirement (total premiums in the first two policy years at least the Planned Periodic Premium) has to be inferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and partly overlaps 3.2(2)'s more detailed pro-rata test, and 2.9 states the same floor differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed pro-rata test — one-twelfth of the annual Planned Periodic Premium times elapsed months, tested at the end of each of the first twenty-four months — that is arithmetically specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates in different words the no-lapse test in 5.10's final paragraph (which subtracts withdrawals and indebtedness), so the two tests are similar but not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A unilateral right to change the Minimum Premium Remittance 'at any time', with notice, is one-sided but plainly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 2.9's requirement that each payment equal the Minimum Premium Remittance shown in Section 1; a changed remittance and a Section 1 figure could diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision reserves broad discretion to limit 'additional premiums' and then narrows it with 'This will happen only if payment ... would ... increase the difference between the death benefit and the Policy Account Value', a condition that is opaque and may swallow or gut the reserved power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 3.3's tax-driven premium cap and with 2.9's invitation to pay excess premium at any time, but no direct contradiction is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limit is tied to external tax law ('Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act of 1982, section 101F of the Internal Revenue Code ... or any future applicable regulations'), and the garbled statutory citation leaves the standard imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a carve-out from 3.2's 'any amount you choose' and from 2.9, which is a designed exception rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introduction is badly garbled and its window ('within five years after the expiration of the Grace Period and prior to the surrender of the Policy') is stated in a scrambled sentence order.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinstating a policy that 5.10(2) says 'will terminate without value' requires reconciliation, and 7.8 separately makes reinstatements contestable for two years.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only 'Receipt of evidence of insurability of th...' survives; whose insurability and to whose satisfaction is not stated in the fragment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2 uses the fuller formula 'evidence of insurability satisfactory to us', so the standard is supplied elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires premium sufficient for 'at least the next two (2) Monthly Insurance Charges', which is a definite quantum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'Section 5.2' for Monthly Insurance Charges, but 5.2 is Interest Rate and the charge is described in 5.3 — a cross-reference that misfits the rest of the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States that pre-lapse Policy Indebtedness is reinstated if not paid; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4's treatment of indebtedness and with 3.4(4) freezing lapse-date values.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Freezes Policy Account Value, indebtedness and Surrender Charges at the values 'in effect when the Policy lapsed'; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'Surrender Charges' while Section 1 and 5.6/5.9 speak of a 'Surrender Fee' and 'Percent of Surrender Fee', a vocabulary mismatch across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated to 'the effective date of the reinstatement will be the Mont[hly Due Date]...', so the trigger is incomplete on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy elsewhere uses Monthly Due Date effective dates (6.2, 6.3), so the missing text is predictable from context.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short absolute bar on reinstatement once the policy has been returned for its surrender value.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 5.8's statement that all insurance terminates on surrender and 3.4's 'prior to the surrender' window.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It promises to pay the Surrender Value 'if the Insured is living and this Policy is in force' without stating that a surrender request is required, and conditions death payment on proof that the Insured died while in force.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.8 supplies the surrender request and the six-month postponement right, and 5.10 governs when the policy is 'in force', so 4.1 is a summary that depends on those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A spendthrift-style sentence expressly limited to 'the extent permitted by law'; the qualifier removes most of the bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses creditors; 8.3's assignment right is a different subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Survives only as a fragment identifying that the amount depends on Specified Amount and Coverage Option in effect at death.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Option A and Option B paragraphs immediately following supply the substance, and Section 1 shows Option A is in effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb 'greater of' formula with a corridor percentage; the arithmetic is spelled out, though 'the correct age of the Insured' depends on the truncated age definition in 2.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the age/percentage table and with 4.2's closing adjustment paragraph; no contradiction found with 2.14 or 2.17.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel to Option A and equally specific, save for the transcription slip 'prior to our coinciding with date of death'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 shows Option A in force, and 6.3 permits a change of option, so Option B's terms are contingent but coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause increases the death benefit by 'any premiums received after the date of death', which is an odd rule and reads against 4.2's Option A limb 1 (premiums received since the prior Monthly Due Date).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also sits against 5.10(3), which deducts unpaid premium from the Proceeds when the Insured dies in the grace period, so premiums cut both ways at death.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A unilateral power to 'modify the death benefits ... in order to comply with Federal tax laws or regulations' paired with the Owner's right to refuse leaves the consequence of refusal unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against 6.4 (changes must be approved and signed by an officer, endorsed on the policy) and against 3.3's tax-qualification cap, without a stated priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest 'at an annual rate determined by us but never less than the rate required by the state in which the Insured resides' hands the insurer discretion above a statutory floor, but the floor is objectively ascertainable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses the Insured's state of residence while 5.6 and 5.11 use the state in which the Policy is delivered — different governing-state references within one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account-value formula 'A + B + C - D - E' survives with its component definitions scrambled and incomplete, so what is added and subtracted cannot be read off the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It labels 'E' the Monthly Insurance Charge 'as described in Section 2', but the charge is defined in 2.15 and described operatively in 5.3, and this value feeds 5.6, 5.7 and the 5.10 lapse test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The worked example is wrong on its face — '6% less 2 points equals 6%' — and the crediting rate is otherwise left to 'the rates declared by us' above the Section 1 guarantee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 9.3's loan interest rate and 5.6's clawback of the excess of credited over guaranteed interest, so the loan-offset arithmetic matters elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sets the monthly charge equal to cost of insurance plus rider costs; the sentence is scrambled by transcription but the rule is simple.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 2.15 and 5.5 and feeds 5.1's deduction; the only friction is 2.15's mis-citation to Section 4.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is stated as due 'on any Premium Due Date' although the policy defines only a Monthly Due Date, the guaranteed maximum table is expressed 'per $1,050' rather than per $1,000, and rates are set by the insurer 'based on our expectation of future experience'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined 'Premium Due Date' has no counterpart in 2.17, 5.3 or 5.10, and the discretionary rate-setting drives the lapse machinery in 5.10 and 9.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The (a)/(b) adjustment for 'special risk classes' is transcribed out of order and incomplete, so the multiplier for a flat extra rating cannot be applied from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 lists the risk class as 'STANDARD' with no substandard or flat extra shown, so the provision has little to bite on here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line referral of rider costs to Section 1; nothing to construe within it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 does show the Waiver of Deduction Rider, and 5.3 adds those costs to the monthly charge, so the referral works.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Cash Value equation is given only as labelled components A, B and C without the operator, and 'C' — the difference between interest actually credited and guaranteed interest over the preceding twelve months — is an unusual deduction whose effect is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cash Value feeds 5.7, 5.9 and 9.4's lapse trigger, and the closing floor keyed to 'the state in which this Policy is delivered' repeats a state reference that 4.3 states differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two lines defining Surrender Value as Cash Value less Policy Indebtedness; arithmetically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reconciles 5.10's Surrender-Value lapse test with 9.4's Cash-Value-less-indebtedness test, so the two lapse formulations collapse into one.
